label: Existence as a predicate, part 1: definitional truth retorsion and nuclear characterization
summary: Existence as a predicate, part 1 (owner-queued slice 3 of 5; #1784, #397). Analyst formulations, attribution deferred; author names (Meinong 1904/1907, Russell 1905, Parsons 1980, Zalta, Kant A598/B626) are navigation only. Vocabulary TruthCore.Ontology.ExistencePredicate, results TruthCore.Results.Ontology.ExistencePredicate, spec specs/existence-predicate.toml. (1) Owner's definitional argument. DefinitionalFrame: objects, an existence predicate Existent marking the beings (Beings F, the domain over which the root's GodExists is read), and a primitive Defined (introduced by stipulation). P1 = DefinesExistingOmnibenevolentGod (the description existing-God-omnibenevolent is defined); P2 weak = DefinitionsAreTrue (every defined description is satisfied); P2 unrestricted = UnrestrictedCharacterization (every description is satisfied). definitionalArgument (zero axioms) derives GodExists over Beings F: valid, registered as a transcription by instantiation, so it adds no support alternative and does not change any route cost (frontier-diff: routes unchanged, three bare premises listed). definitionalTruthRetorsion (premise-free, zero axioms): (a) the unrestricted principle is logically false in every frame (a single instance fails); (b) if 'the existing being that is the only God and is omnibenevolent' and the same 'and is not omnibenevolent' are both defined, the weak P2 fails (its contrary instances clash: uniqueness identifies the two satisfiers); (c) each description is satisfiable in some frame, so the clash is not a single self-contradictory description; (d) P1 and the weak P2 hold together in a one-object frame defining only P1's description, so they are jointly consistent. Relations: the retorsion refutes the unrestricted P2 (counted: refuted_statements) and attacks the weak P2; strengthens unrestricted -> weak (unrestrictedGivesDefinitionsTrue). Finding: P1 and the weak P2 are jointly consistent, but the freedom of stipulation P1 uses also licenses the contrary sole-God definition, under which the weak P2 is contradictory. So P2 gets no warrant from definitional freedom, and a P2 restricted enough to stay consistent must exclude descriptions for reasons other than their having been defined (as the nuclear reconstruction does); that restriction must already decide which descriptions are satisfied, which is the existence question itself: existence cannot be put into a definition and taken out as a fact. Analytic reading (sibling statement): 'whatever satisfies a defined description satisfies it' is true by stipulation and has no existential import; analyticReadingCountermodel (zero axioms; one nonexistent object, everything defined) satisfies P1 and the analytic P2 with no being God, so the argument is invalid under that reading. This parallels the repository rule against hiding bridges in definitions. The naive P2 is not presented as Meinong's view. (2) Parsons-style nuclear characterization. ParsonsFrame: objects, nuclear properties, HasNuclear, extranuclear existence ExistsExtranuclear (EXISTENCE_4, appended to DISAMB-RUSSELL-EXISTENCE) and the watered-down nuclear 'existent' (NuclearExistent, EXISTENCE_5). NuclearCharacterization: every set of nuclear properties is the nuclear set of exactly one object. nuclearCharacterizationControl (premise-free; propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound via Mathlib Set): (a) in every frame satisfying it, an object with given nuclear g, o and EXISTENCE_5 exists as an object; (b) the model with objects = sets of {god, benevolent, existent} and extranuclear existents = nuclear-existent non-gods satisfies the principle, has existents, has the nuclear-existent god object, has no EXISTENCE_4 god; its definitional frame (Defined = nuclear descriptions, Existent = EXISTENCE_4) satisfies the weak P2 while P1's description is not a nuclear (admissible) description there (in this model EXISTENCE_4 is not closed under adding nuclear properties) and GodExists over its beings fails; every stipulation practice satisfying the open bridge StipulationsAdmissible (every stipulated description is admissible) leaves P1's description unstipulated. In nuclearDefinitionalFrame, Defined is read as admissibility, not stipulation; the bridge statement keeps the two readings apart; (c) naming question: with InAct x esse read as EXISTENCE_5, MoreIn ranking the god object above all, and trivial CausesIn, the naming premise's form GodNamesTheUniqueMaximeEns holds, the god object is the unique maximum in being and causes all in the genus, GodExists over objects holds, and still no EXISTENCE_4 god exists. Finding for the naming premises: only e39a4fce is model-checked (its form holds in the model). The route's existential import comes from the maximum-existence premise (InAct m esse inside IsMaximumIn) together with the carrier; with an object-theory carrier, InAct _ esse must carry EXISTENCE_4 (or the route's own act/esse sense of existence among beings), not a characterizing property, or the naming bridge delivers a nonexistent god object. 1ec205ed is a nominal definition of the same conditional shape and 957a71fe is a derived statement (result AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-MAXIME-ENS-IS-GOD), not a nominal definition; the claim that neither carries existential import of its own rests on inspection of their Lean types (both are universally quantified conditionals over IsMaximumIn), not on a model check. The control is one formal interpretation; it is not evidence that object theory is true or that esse is nuclear. The control attacks the open bridge StipulationsAdmissible (relation 6cc0f63d, retargeted from P1 after review; its note states target, mechanism, the side condition that EXISTENCE_4 is not closed under adding nuclear properties in the model, justification, and scope: one reconstruction, not a checked dilemma over all restrictions). Rejected readings: (i) P2 as Meinong's characterization principle (Meinong restricts characterization to nuclear/constitutive properties; the naive principle is Russell's 1905 target); (ii) Prop-valued sets with uniqueness without Mathlib (needs propext/funext; used Mathlib Set instead, permitted axioms only in the Parsons result); (iii) concluding the definitional argument's full omnibenevolence triple and registering a strength order to STMT-GOD-EXISTS (a non-transcription weakening from a bare leaf would have made GodExists a one-leaf expansion and falsely lowered route costs). Not delivered (file budget; next tests): (A) Zalta abstract object theory: Object = ordinary + abstract, Encodes vs Exemplifies, object comprehension over encoded properties; show consistency, that the comprehended abstract object encoding {God, omnibenevolent, E!} encodes E! but does not exemplify E! (abstract objects do not exemplify concreteness), and relate encoded vs exemplified 'God' to the naming bridge; new senses EXISTENCE_6 (exemplified E!) and EXISTENCE_7 (encoded E!) with distinct Lean declarations. (B) Kant, existence not a real predicate (A598/B626): sense fork against EXISTENCE_1 (positing/instantiation of a concept) with sibling statements; target analysis: Kant's thesis targets steps that treat existence as a content of a concept, namely the ontological premise that the concept of the most real being includes existence and, via A606-608, the cosmological identification NecessaryIsMostReal whose conversion needs it (existing result CONVERSION-NEEDS-EXISTENCE). The root's quarta-via and prima-via routes do not use such a step: their existence comes from a posteriori premises, and naming is conditional, as the Parsons control shows formally; Kant's separate scope objection to those premises is already recorded in docs/kant-cosmological-inference.md. Connection plan for (B): relate the RealityProfile features of TruthCore.German.Kant.CosmologicalInference to a 'not a real predicate' statement (existence is not among the positive features) and test whether IdentificationNeedsBridge/conversion results depend on it.
